correctness.rationale: The claim follows from an exact beta-moment/Jacobi polynomial diagonalization, a uniform Gaussian domination for k above n^(3/5), a three-order logarithmic expansion centered at k+(a+b+1)/2, and shifted Euler–Maclaurin summation. The Gaussian integrals give both coefficients; all errors are uniform on compact parameter sets. Extracted checker.py passed 28 exact rational spectral identities, 19 exact trace identities, and 24 finite-dimensional asymptotic comparisons. Those tests are not the infinite proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Taking k fixed in the prior eigenvalue expansion is insufficient for k of order sqrt(n), which contributes the full leading spectral trace. The prior exact eigenvalues permit a new asymptotic derivation but do not imply the displayed three terms without the uniform moving-window analysis. No published broader power-trace theorem was found that subsumes these coefficients.

value.rationale: The theorem completely describes the first three terms of a natural family of Schatten-power moments of the classical selfadjoint approximation operator for every fixed real Jacobi weight and every positive exponent. It exposes a power-independent Jacobi boundary term, an unweighted cancellation, and an explicit subsequent coefficient, with compact-uniform error. These are structurally relevant for comparisons of effective spectral dimension and Hilbert–Schmidt energy and are not a single artificial parameter computation.
